lesson.title: Who wrote this? Detectors and fair rules
lesson.subtitle: A score is a guess, never proof

video.title: Who wrote this? Detectors and fair rules
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: A pupil's essay; “92% AI”; She wrote it herself.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A colleague ran a pupil's essay through an AI detector. It said ninety-two percent AI. The girl cried, because she had written every word herself.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how AI detectors guess, why a score is never proof, and fair rules for AI in your class.

scenes.visual: A list: It can't see who wrote it; It looks for even, predictable words; A score is a guess.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: An AI detector can't see who wrote a text. It looks for patterns that machine writing often has, like very even, predictable words. Then it gives a score: a guess, not a fact.

scenes.visual: A list: A hidden watermark; It prefers “green” words; A detector with the key counts; Lots of green: probably AI.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some AI makers add a hidden watermark. The model quietly prefers certain words, its green list, and a detector with the key counts them. Lots of green words means it was probably the machine.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: But a score is never proof. Honest writing is sometimes flagged by chance. Editing two or three words can erase a watermark. And studies found that detectors flag people writing in a second language more often.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A detector says a pupil's homework is ninety-two percent AI. What should happen next?

scenes.visual: A list: Talk with the pupil; Notes and drafts; A short paragraph in class; A score never decides alone.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Talk with the pupil. Ask them to explain their work, show their notes or a draft, or write a short paragraph in class. A pupil who wrote it can usually tell you how. A score alone should never decide a mark.

scenes.visual: A list: When AI is allowed; When it isn't; How to show you used it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Better still, set the rules before anyone is accused. Say when AI is allowed, when it isn't, and how to show it was used. Pupils who know the rules rarely need a detector.

scenes.visual: A list: Keep it out; Check it; Verify it; Be fair; Tell someone.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Put the whole unit together as five class rules. Keep it out: no secrets. Check it: by the stakes. Verify it: on a second channel. Be fair: nobody is accused on a score. And tell someone when something goes wrong.

scenes.visual: A list: Rules on the wall; In the pupils' own words; Safe to tell.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In my class the rules are on the wall, in the pupils' own words. When something goes wrong, they know they can tell me without getting into trouble.

scenes.visual: A list: Write with the watermark; Honest text, sometimes flagged; Edit a few words: it fades.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, write with the watermark and watch the detector count the green words. Then write naturally a few times: now and then, an honest sentence gets flagged. Finally, edit a few words and watch the signal fade.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which of these is a fair class rule about AI?

scenes.visual: The summary: A score is a guess; Honest writing gets flagged; Talk before you judge; Five class rules. Takeaway: Be fair: a score never decides alone.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Say when you used AI, and be ready to explain: that's clear and fair. Remember: a detector's score is a guess, and honest writing gets flagged. Talk before you judge, and agree five rules with your class.

scenes.visual: A list: Write the rules together; In pupils' own words; Put them on the wall.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: write your five AI rules together. Take each rule in turn and let pupils put it in their own words. Then put the rules on the wall, where everyone can see them.

checkpoints.prompt: A detector says a pupil's homework is 92% AI. What should happen next?

options.text: Talk with the pupil and ask them to explain their work
Run other detectors until one agrees

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right: a score is a guess. Talk first, and look at the pupil's work and drafts.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: a score is never proof, and more detectors only add guesses. Talk with the pupil.

checkpoints.prompt: Which of these is a fair class rule about AI?

options.text: “Say when you used AI, and be ready to explain your work.”
“If the AI says it's right, it's right.”

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes: it's clear, fair, and doesn't rest on a guess.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: a score is a guess, and AI can be wrong. A fair rule asks pupils to say and explain.
